summary: std::make_unique creates a unique_ptr with exception-safe construction. It constructs an object and wraps it in a std::unique_ptr, providing memory safety and preventing leaks when exceptions are thrown.
cpp17_notes: C++17 improves unique_ptr with constexpr support. C++20 adds make_unique_for_overwrite for default-initialized (uninitialized) objects. Array support with make_unique<T[]> is fully available.
audio_thread_notes: std::make_unique MUST NOT be called from the audio thread. It allocates heap memory. Pre-allocate unique_ptr instances during initialization. unique_ptr itself is fine to use on audio thread if already constructed - just don't reset() or release() to allocate.
